kelvaroq.name: Kelvaroq
kelvaroq.summary: Kelvaroq is a public Rust runtime built on VIctory and victory-fork. It adds rendering patches and measured submission improvements, and runs GTA VI through the prologue and first mission.

victory-nvidia.name: VIctory-NVIDIA
victory-nvidia.summary: An NVIDIA fork of VIctory on readmet3xt-lab's foxhound, with DLSS, frame generation and an in-game settings menu. PortWatch has verified it: about as playable as the leaders, at 20 fps without frame generation and without crashes.

belobug.name: Belobug
belobug.nuked_note: Repository and GitHub account removed by GitHub on Nov 27 for a Terms of Service violation, confirmed by PortWatch. Its progress still counts in our overall number.
belobug.summary: Belobug's VIctory fork for AMD Radeon is very playable: about 22 fps on average with no crashes, and story progress rated 80%. Its code and GitHub account were removed by GitHub on 27 Nov for a Terms of Service violation, which PortWatch has confirmed.

dexnom.name: DexNom
dexnom.summary: DexNom Runtime, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon, tested on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX. It builds on ZSlayerHQ's victory-world-runtime with its own fixes for shaders, texture streaming and GPU memory. PortWatch has seen it running with ray-traced lighting working, the first AMD build on our board to get it. Its picture is the best-rated on our board, though lighting and materials still have problems, and it plays through missions at about 3-4 fps (about 1 fps with ray tracing on), rarely crashing.

zettrox.name: ZETTROX
zettrox.nuked_note: GitHub repo and the Zettrox account gone on Nov 25 (HTTP 404 by 17:26 UTC). No DMCA notice is published yet.
zettrox.summary: ZETTROX's build of VIctory and hyphennn's victory-fork for NVIDIA cards. It plays from Lucia's prologue into Jason's first mission, "Gone Fishing", where PortWatch verified the first kill with a gun in GTA VI on PC. Rendering is still poor and it runs at about 2 fps, but it's playable and almost never crashes.

vitoriabr.name: Uilian
vitoriabr.summary: Uilian's VItoriaBr, built on hyphennn's victory-fork with his own NVIDIA work and streamed live on YouTube. On stream it reaches Jason's first mission, "Gone Fishing", with poor rendering, up to 4 fps and few crashes.

avatarmanz.name: AvatarManz
avatarmanz.nuked_note: Repository and GitHub account removed by GitHub on Nov 27 for a Terms of Service violation, as with Belobug, confirmed by PortWatch. Its progress still counts in our overall number.
avatarmanz.summary: AvatarManz's VIctory fork for the AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX, verified by PortWatch at about 16 fps on average, with sound. Its code and GitHub account were removed by GitHub on 27 Nov for a Terms of Service violation, as Belobug's were, which PortWatch has confirmed.

notnozy.name: NotNozy
notnozy.summary: A private build shown on NotNozy's "GTA6 Modding Stream" on Rumble. It looks about the same as AvatarManz's build; the owner rates its story progress at 80%. It runs on an AMD card. Code not public, and what it builds on isn't known.

doomsday.name: Doomsday
doomsday.summary: A private group's build on JoshuuDev's victory-amd fork of VIctory, verified by PortWatch. It runs GTA VI with ray-traced lighting at about 3-5 fps, almost never crashes, and the owner rates its story progress at 80%. The in-game phone renders really well, and the map menu runs at a higher frame rate. It's built mostly for AMD and also works on NVIDIA, at a lower frame rate. Code not public.

darkworldhm.name: darkworldhm
darkworldhm.summary: A build shown on darkworldhm's Rumble stream on 25 Nov, running GTA VI's free roam at about 12-15 fps, swinging between 5 and 24: the highest frame rate on our board. The owner rates its story progress at 80%, and it hasn't crashed so far. The picture looks alright, with some texture or ray-tracing glitches. Reportedly on an NVIDIA RTX 50-series card. It's built on VIctory, but which fork isn't known. Code not public.

suri.name: suri
suri.summary: A private build on hyphennn's victory-fork of VIctory. PortWatch confirmed a player moving around Lucia's prologue at about 3 fps; the owner now rates its story progress at 80%. Code is not public.

omonkey.name: omonkey
omonkey.nuked_note: Taken down on Nov 25 (the owner's report). Its code was never public; Swaggely's Rumble channel, where it was streamed, still loaded at 18:18 UTC.
omonkey.summary: A developer who streams all his work live on Rumble, through Swaggely's channel. GTA VI's shaders have started loading properly, and a player moves slowly around the opening prison scene at about 5 fps. No public code.

cgbj.name: CGBJ
cgbj.summary: Private VIctory/XCL build, PortWatch-verified. Owner rates story progress at 80%, rendering 0.7 and stability 0.85. It averages 25 fps with 8 GB system RAM and 16 GB VRAM. Its code was public briefly and is offline now.

victory-gta6.name: hyphennn
victory-gta6.summary: hyphennn's fork of VIctory (formerly victory-gta6), with his own rendering and speed fixes. On his Rumble streams the prologue plays with ray-traced lighting, detailed textures and hair at about 3 fps; the README still lists shadows as black. Self-reported.

marvis.name: VIctory
marvis.summary: Marvis's Rust layer runs GTA VI natively. The owner reports controlled gameplay is now reachable, though the build remains unstable; the README still says it is not playable and reports about 1 fps in the world.

xbox-emulator.name: xbox-emulator
xbox-emulator.summary: Rust runtime that runs dumped Xbox Series builds as normal Windows processes, continuing the TomBox project. It reports Trackmania races driving at about 60 fps and Terraria reaching its world, plus Fortnite's lobby. Self-reported.

xcl.name: XCL
xcl.summary: Wine-style layer running game code natively. On its main branch GTA VI gets past its menus into the world for several testers, but the screen stays on a loading spinner and a GPU watchdog ends the run. Unverified.

scarlettx.name: ScarlettX
scarlettx.summary: Clean-room high-level emulator of the Scarlett OS and GDK runtime. It reports two retail Xbox Series games, Concept Destruction and Unicorn Overlord, playable on Windows.

tuxbox.name: TuxBox
tuxbox.summary: Native-first layer for unpacked Xbox Series games, tested mostly on Linux through Proton. GTA VI reported its own state as "Game Running" in the story intro before crashing after about ten minutes, but no picture past the player-selection prompt is shown. Self-reported.

americas-recomp.name: americas-recomp
americas-recomp.nuked_note: GitHub repo gone since about 22:00 UTC on Nov 23 (HTTP 404). Its owner's account is still active and no DMCA notice is published, so it was likely deleted or made private.
americas-recomp.summary: Fork of AnyPS5 that tested whether the PS5 port tool's RDNA2 shader recompiler can handle the Xbox game. Taken offline on Nov 23: the repo answers 404, its owner's account is still active, and no DMCA notice is published.

leonida.name: Leonida
leonida.nuked_note: Discord gone, GitHub repo deleted and creator quit on Nov 23. On Nov 24 a Take-Two DMCA notice disabled its network of 3,007 GitHub forks; separately uploaded copies and a frozen mirror remain.
leonida.summary: Made just for GTA VI, by Hookshot's author. Taken offline on Nov 23: its Discord vanished, the GitHub repo was deleted and the creator said he quit. Last result: the exe ran, frames stayed black.

openscarlett.name: OpenScarlett
openscarlett.summary: MIT-licensed C++20 translation layer targeting D3D12 and Vulkan. It now claims 17 boot stops cleared on a retail title it doesn't name, with no run record or frame shown, so no GTA VI milestone yet.

scarlett-layer.name: scarlett-layer
scarlett-layer.summary: Loader plus injected hook DLL that redirects console-only calls to Windows shims, with its own d3d12_xs wrapper and shader lifter. It reports Terraria's GDK build rendering its menus with audio; no gameplay yet.

xbox2windows.name: Xbox2Windows
xbox2windows.summary: Static recompilation research turning Xbox Series code and shaders into Windows C++ and DXIL, with over 50 contributors. Footage the project shared shows GTA VI's menus, unstable. Its README now reports a modified diagnostic exe playing the intro and setup text; the original exe and the menus remain unverified.

anyxboxx.name: AnyXboxX
anyxboxx.summary: French-language prototype: GDK runtime emulation on Unicorn, plus a Wine-style native mode that runs small GDK test games. Its GTA VI results (world at about 5 fps, cutscenes, a contributor's report of the first two missions) come from victory-fork's code, now copied into the repo, so they earn it no milestone.

keylime.name: keylime
keylime.summary: A C++20 runtime written from scratch, with Vulkan graphics and its own RDNA2-to-SPIR-V translator. It reports GTA VI's intro and main menu at 30 fps and the world loading into the opening cutscene, which doesn't draw yet. Self-reported.

xvalkyrie.name: XValkyrie
xvalkyrie.summary: Wine-style C++ layer for Xbox One and Series titles with native code and RDNA2-to-HLSL shaders. It now calls Minecraft Preview and Unicorn Overlord playable, though its Minecraft note describes only the main menu. Unverified.

gtavi-recomp.name: GTAVI-Recomp
gtavi-recomp.summary: Targets the PS5 build through AnyPS5 and will not work from leaked files, so game research is blocked. Work continues on AnyPS5 itself.

anyxboxseries.name: AnyXboxSeries
anyxboxseries.summary: GTA VI-only translation layer with a PE mapper borrowed from Xbox2Windows, an early scalar shader lifter and a sample game that tests presentation and input.

scarab.name: SCARAB
scarab.summary: Found that the console d3d12_xs uses the same 28 interface IDs as PC D3D12, so standard calls can be forwarded and only the console extensions need building.

anybox.name: AnyBox
anybox.summary: Relinks GDK executables against reimplemented system libraries, AnyPS5-style. The pipeline works end to end on a test title.

percyscarlett.name: PercyScarlett
percyscarlett.summary: Rust layer with stand-in system DLLs and an early shader recompiler. GTA VI now runs to a frame loop of black frames, then the GPU hangs. Its shader path still uses stand-ins, and its stage counts don't match other projects'.

grandtheftxbox.name: GrandTheftXbox
grandtheftxbox.summary: Wine-style layer planned for Series and One titles. Sits between milestones 0 and 1, and has been quiet since Nov 20.

scarlett-windows-compat.name: Scarlett Windows Compat
scarlett-windows-compat.summary: Clean-room test programs for how Game Core software meets Windows, covering loading, memory, presentation and input, plus a radar that watches other projects.

dedsec.name: DedSec
dedsec.summary: Portuguese-language GTA VI port targeting DirectX 12 with an RDNA2-to-HLSL translator. Most of its files sit at the same paths as Leonida's, 86 of them identical, and its README doesn't credit Leonida. It does not boot.

xbgtasix.name: Xbgtasix
xbgtasix.summary: Chinese-language layer that places stand-in xgameruntime, xmem and d3d12_xs DLLs next to an executable, plus sourced research notes on the archive, shader and texture formats.

seriesx-emulator.name: SeriesX Emulator
seriesx-emulator.summary: C++ emulator that interprets x86-64 code instead of running it natively, with a launcher and seven XGameRuntime functions. Only programs it builds itself run; it says no commercial game works.

gta6-compat-layer.name: GTA6-COMPAT-LAYER (ScarlettCompat)
gta6-compat-layer.summary: C++ layer with its own PE loader and Xbox function registry. Its README now reports GTA VI's exe loading with all 587 imports and running its startup into pipeline creation over 113 boots; no frame yet. Self-reported.

xlaunchvi.name: XlaunchVI
xlaunchvi.summary: Multi-contributor C++ layer with a PE loader, a D3D12 backend and an RDNA2 shader translator that matches AMD-compiled test shaders bit for bit. Most code sits in open pull requests, and no Xbox title has run.

openscarlett-ce.name: OpenScarlett (Community Edition)
openscarlett-ce.summary: AGPL C++ layer, separate from the other OpenScarlett, that swaps console DLLs for PC Direct3D 12 ones and translates console GPU code. It reports Minecraft Preview playable at about 60 fps, and an unnamed newer retail game reaching its start screen. Self-reported; no GTA VI credit until it names the game's files.

port-of-the-americas.name: Port of the Americas
port-of-the-americas.summary: Linux layer that runs GTA VI's own exe under Proton with replacement console DLLs on a patched vkd3d-proton. Its repo shows the player-selection prompt and loading screens; the world draws black. Shader translation leans on Leonida's. Self-reported.

five-star-recomp.name: Five Star Recomp
five-star-recomp.summary: C# layer and toolkit for GTA VI. It reports the game loading story mode and playing the opening cutscene's title cards, dialogue and sound at 30 fps, but the cutscene's 3D world doesn't draw yet. Self-reported; no capture.

g6recomp.name: G6Recomp
g6recomp.summary: Carefully tested C++ loader and console-runtime rewrite for GTA VI, with its own code throughout. The game's side DLLs initialise under it; shaders are only decoded so far and there is no graphics layer yet.

gta6-boottest.name: GTA6-BootTest
gta6-boottest.summary: C stand-in DLLs and a debugger harness that run GTA VI's exe on Windows through its frame loop. It says the first UI screen now draws on a PC GPU, but shows no capture yet. Self-reported.

palmetto.name: Palmetto
palmetto.summary: Open continuation of Leonida after its repo went private. It reports GTA VI's exe running past 300 s, executing its draws and presenting to its own window, but every frame reads back black. Self-reported, one RTX 4090.

pinned.text:
**Why the top score is stuck at 91.3%: it's rendering now, not FPS.**

FPS is the easy part. Turn off ray tracing, render at a low resolution and upscale, and you can hit 60. On our scale anything past 30 fps doesn't count, and a blurry low-res picture costs rendering points.

What's missing is a picture that looks like the console: full lighting, ray tracing, sharp textures. Like DexNom said, the way forward is fixing rendering.
